topStories.headline: Waymo Wins Statewide Expansion Approval — and Market Street Rideshare Pilot Goes Live
topStories.dek: Two milestones in the same week cement San Francisco's role as the proving ground for autonomous vehicles, with new pick-up zones on Market Street and a sweeping CPUC green light for Bay Area-wide service.
topStories.body:
The California Public Utilities Commission granted Waymo approval on August 14 to expand its fully driverless ride-hailing service across 18 counties, clearing the company to operate throughout the entire San Francisco Bay Area and to launch new markets in Sacramento and San Diego. The approval covers territory from Sonoma County south to the Mexican border, making it the largest regulatory step in the company's history. Waymo said expansion would be gradual and guided by its safety framework, with an immediate focus on launching rider-only service in San Diego later this summer.

The CPUC milestone landed just as a separate local pilot kicked into gear. Beginning August 26, the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency launched an evaluation allowing Waymo — along with a limited number of Uber Black and Lyft Black vehicles — to pick up and drop off passengers at up to seven designated bays along a two-mile stretch of Market Street during set hours. Market Street has been closed to private cars since 2020. Mayor Daniel Lurie framed the pilot as a tool for revitalizing the downtown corridor.

For SoMa residents and commuters, the combined news means more autonomous vehicle activity along the neighborhood's northern and western edges. Critics from transit and pedestrian advocacy groups have warned that introducing any vehicle traffic to the car-free stretch risks undermining Muni performance and pedestrian safety gains built over two decades. The SFMTA said it will monitor traffic conditions, safety incidents, and rideshare performance through shared data and street-level observation throughout the evaluation period.

Waymo's fleet has now logged more than 20 million trips across its U.S. markets and is targeting one million rides per week by year's end. The CPUC approval follows the California DMV's authorization of the same expanded service area last year.

topStories.headline: Treasure Island Redevelopment Makes National Headlines as First Residents Move In
topStories.dek: A Washington Post feature this week spotlighted new apartments and condominiums now open on the 576-acre former Navy base, marking a turning point for one of the city's longest-running housing projects.
topStories.body:
Treasure Island's long-promised transformation is no longer a plan on paper. The Washington Post published a major feature on August 21 documenting the arrival of the first wave of residents in new apartments and condominiums on the 576-acre island that the U.S. Navy abandoned nearly 30 years ago. The piece landed as the island's redevelopment reaches a visible milestone: completed buildings, open parks, and an operating ferry terminal.

Phase one of the redevelopment was formally completed in July with the opening of 490 Avenue of the Palms, a six-story, 148-unit condominium complex co-developed by Lennar Corporation, Stockbridge Capital Group, and Wilson Meany. It is the first condominium building constructed on Treasure Island. Separately, Star View Court — a seven-story, 138-unit building of permanently affordable apartments — is also open, providing homes for people exiting homelessness and qualifying local residents. The island's affordable housing portfolio is designed to eventually deliver more than 2,000 below-market homes.

At full build-out, the Treasure Island and Yerba Buena Island development program envisions 8,000 to 10,800 housing units, with 27 percent affordable, along with approximately 300 acres of parks and open space. A revised proposal from earlier this year proposed increasing density by up to 35 percent and shifting more units from for-sale condominiums to rental apartments, which can be built faster. The island already has a ferry terminal offering a roughly 10-minute ride to the Ferry Building, and new roads, utilities, and waterfront parks have been built as part of more than $800 million in infrastructure investment.

Sheela Jivan, appointed in May as the new executive director of the Treasure Island Development Authority, is overseeing the next phases. Mayor Lurie has called the project critical to San Francisco meeting its state-mandated housing production targets.

topStories.headline: SF's First Artist Housing Tower Breaks Ground on Mid-Market — City Now Must Define Who Qualifies
topStories.dek: The Artists Hub on Market project at 1687 Market Street officially broke ground in late July, but the city is still building the certification process that will decide which San Franciscans can call themselves artists.
topStories.body:
San Francisco broke ground on July 28 on the Artists Hub on Market, a 15-story, $140 million mixed-use tower at 1687 Market Street, making it the city's first affordable housing development reserved specifically for artists and arts workers. The project, co-developed by nonprofit Mercy Housing California and Artists Hub on Market — a nonprofit co-founded by SFJazz founder Randall Kline — will deliver 94 permanently affordable apartments alongside rehearsal studios, a black-box theater, office and program space for arts organizations, and a ground-floor café open to the community. The building is expected to open in 2028.

The tower sits at the corner of Market and Gough streets, on a site that formerly housed a McRoskey Mattress showroom. It is centrally positioned at the intersection of Hayes Valley, Civic Center, the Mission, and the Castro — and within SoMa's broader orbit — giving it access to a dense network of arts organizations and transit lines. Income caps vary by unit and household size, with set-asides for households earning 30, 60, and 80 percent of area median income.

A complication has emerged: San Francisco is still constructing the formal Artist Housing Certification Program that will determine who qualifies as an artist for the purposes of applying. The SF Chronicle reported this week that the city is working to create a first-of-its-kind credentialing process, and artists can submit interest forms now even as the full application process remains under development. City Arts and Culture Executive Director Matthew Goudeau has described the project as a way to ensure the people who shape San Francisco's cultural life can afford to remain in the city.

events.title: SFMOMA: Matisse's Femme au chapeau — A Modern Scandal
events.description: The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art presents a major exhibition tracing the history and enduring influence of Matisse's 1905 portrait of his wife Amélie, positioning it in dialogue with his peers and with artists working today including Bay Area Figurative masters Joan Brown and Richard Diebenkorn. The museum's Thursday Night programming on September 3 includes an opening celebration for a new show, 'In Between,' from 6–8 p.m.

events.title: 65th Annual Potrero Hill Artists' Exhibition
events.location: Potrero Hill Branch Library, Potrero Hill
events.description: The Potrero Hill Branch Library hosts its 65th annual exhibition of artwork by library patrons who live, learn, work, or worship on Potrero Hill and Dogpatch. The show closes Saturday, August 29.

events.title: Yerba Buena Gardens Festival — Ongoing Free Performances

events.description: Now in its 26th season, the Yerba Buena Gardens Festival continues through November with over 100 free outdoor performances including world music, dance, theater, and children's programming. Upcoming highlights include Los Calderones (September 3, 6–7:30 p.m.) and a free outdoor movie night (September 5, 7–9:30 p.m.).

events.title: Hayden James Sunset Party at Aracely Garden
events.description: Australian producer and DJ Hayden James headlines a sunset dance party at the Aracely Garden on Treasure Island, an open-air garden venue with sweeping views of the San Francisco skyline.

events.title: Treasure Island Yacht Club Chili Cook-Off
events.location: Treasure Island Yacht Club, Treasure Island
events.description: Bring your best recipe and compete for the top prize ($10 to enter), or pay $20 to sample all entries and help crown the winner at this lively community cook-off on Treasure Island.

events.title: SOMA Nights Block Party & Night Market
events.description: The final installment of the 2026 SOMA Nights series brings a free monthly street party back to the Folsom Corridor, with local food vendors, pop-up shops, art, DJs, and activations from more than 20 neighborhood businesses. (The August 27 edition concluded the previous week; September 24 is the next and final date.)

events.title: Potrero Hill R&B Festival — 51st Year
events.location: 20th Street between Wisconsin & Missouri Sts., Potrero Hill
events.description: The 51st annual Potrero Hill R&B Festival returns with live music on two stages, local food and craft vendors, and family activities across four blocks of 20th Street; the free festival benefits Daniel Webster and Starr King Elementary Schools and the Potrero Hill Neighborhood House.

moreNews.headline: Potrero Annex Demolition Continues as HOPE SF Rebuild Advances
moreNews.body: Demolition of the Potrero Annex public housing complex — a World War II-era development at 700 Missouri Street in Potrero Hill — has been underway since spring 2026, marking a long-delayed milestone in the HOPE SF program. The roughly 619 units across 23 buildings in the Annex are being cleared to make way for a mixed-income project of up to 1,700 new units. The Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development said next-phase demolition work would focus on buildings on Turner Terrace, Watchman Way, and Missouri Street. The full rebuild is expected to take 10 to 12 years.

moreNews.headline: Ruth Asawa Gallery Opens Permanent Home at Minnesota Street Project
moreNews.body: Ruth Asawa Lanier, Inc. opened a permanent dedicated gallery for the beloved San Francisco artist at Minnesota Street Project in Dogpatch in May, occupying the 1,714-square-foot downstairs space previously held by Anglim/Trimble. The gallery is billed as the first permanent public venue dedicated to Asawa's wire sculptures, drawings, and community-oriented practice — a stable street-level home in a city dotted with the artist's public fountains and commissions. The opening came as the Dogpatch arts campus navigated a period of gallery turnover, with new tenants including Art of Contemporary Africa also taking up residence alongside the project's resident galleries.

moreNews.headline: Treasure Island Ferry Service, Events Scene Grow Alongside New Residents
moreNews.body: As more residents move into newly completed buildings on Treasure Island, the island's amenity and events calendar is keeping pace. The Treasure Island SF events site lists ongoing weekend music at Mersea Restaurant (free, Fridays through Sundays), live jazz and cocktails at the Gold Bar Whiskey Distillery — set inside a 1930s Art Deco building — and a growing schedule of community gatherings. The ferry terminal, which opened in 2022, connects the island to the Ferry Building in roughly 10 minutes, making the new neighborhood viable for daily commuters.

restaurants.name: Chez Maman

hotels.name: Canopy by Hilton San Francisco SoMa
hotels.description: A design-forward Hilton lifestyle brand property in SoMa, praised for its welcoming atmosphere and proximity to Yerba Buena Gardens and public transit.

hotels.name: W San Francisco

hotels.name: YOTEL San Francisco

shops.name: Rickshaw Bagworks
shops.description: A San Francisco–made bag manufacturer and retail shop on 22nd Street in Dogpatch, offering messenger bags, laptop sleeves, and custom bags produced in the neighborhood.

shops.name: Heath Ceramics

shops.name: Dandelion Chocolate

shops.name: Creativity Explored
shops.type: Art nonprofit gallery and gift shop

shops.name: SOMArts Cultural Center Shop

shops.name: MAC (Modern Appealing Clothing)

artEntertainment.name: The Midway

artEntertainment.name: Yerba Buena Gardens Festival (Outdoor Stage)

artEntertainment.name: Treasure Island Museum

artEntertainment.name: Little Raven Gallery
artEntertainment.description: An intimate SoMa gallery at 1015 Howard Street presenting contemporary works with regular exhibition openings.
